text:
Ryan Nugent-Hopkins passed Kevin Lowe on Nov. 3 to become the Oilers' all-time leader in games played, and he marked the night against New Jersey with a power-play goal. Four days later he lasted 6.6 minutes against Vancouver; NHL.com reported he was struck in the head by a puck. On Monday he wore a bubble at morning skate, per Daily Faceoff Edmonton, and was listed as good to go against the Rangers.

He has played 9 of Edmonton's 18 games, and his 11 points lean heavily on the power play: 7 of them. At five-on-five the picture is weaker. The Oilers get under 45% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, about five points worse than their share without him, a long way from what McDavid and Draisaitl are doing.

His shooting won't last either: 4 goals on 16 shots is 25%, and our range has his finishing closer to 14%. Expect the power-play points to keep coming, and the even-strength numbers to decide how high in the lineup he stays.
headline: Nugent-Hopkins sets the Oilers record, then a scare
